newsitem.title: MEXICO: Unilever buys 20 pct of Bimbo subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Unilever buys 20 pct of Bimbo subsidiary.

text.p: Mexico's Grupo Industrial Bimbo on Thursday said it had sold a 20 percent stake in ice cream maker Friser to Unilever.
Bimbo, did not reveal the amount involved in the sale, but sector sources estimated it was worth some $70 million.
The agreement required prior agreement by the Mexican Monopolies Commission, as Unilever, an Anglo-Dutch group, will manage 50 percent of Friser's business.
The remaining 50 percent will be run by Bimbo and its partner Grupo Quan, which manufactures and distributes ice cream and popsicles in Mexico and Central America under the Holanda and Bing brands.
Unilever sells frozen foods in Mexico prepared by its Anderson Clayton division, in addition to Ponds health-care products, Marga brand margarine for catering and cold cuts under the Zwan brand.

Unilever announced plans last week to strengthen its position in Mexico, which included rights to the margarine brand Iberia. It said it had struck a deal with Prolesa for its existing Anderson Clayton business.
